title: Philip Selway - Wikipedia
notes: Philip James Selway, born 23 May 1967, Abingdon, Oxfordshire. Began drums and guitar at 15; earliest influences Joy Division, the Clash and the Velvet Underground; called Blondie's Clem Burke his 'drummer hero'. Met the others at Abingdon School; On a Friday from 1985; Radiohead from 1991. Studied English and history at Liverpool Polytechnic; pit bands for touring musicals. From Kid A (2000) drum machines entered the music, which he said widened his options; on Idioteque live: 'Trying to give that sense of the electronic in the piece but doing it through your normal instrument playing.' Clive Deamer a second drummer on the King of Limbs and Moon Shaped Pool tours, Chris Vatalaro in 2025. Gigwise's 26th-greatest drummer (2008), for his 'mathematical precision'; Ed O'Brien: 'Philip has this incredible groove, and he has this weight to what he does.' Solo albums Familial (2010), Weatherhouse (2014), Strange Dance (2023); 7 Worlds Collide; a Samaritans listener for 17 years.

title: Where do we go from here? (Rhythm, July 2001; transcribed at Citizen Insane)
notes: On his style: 'There might be bits of soul drumming and hip-hop and even lighter jazz things all swimming around within my drumming, which is the context of something that is, broadly, a rock band. But none of those styles is a carbon copy.' Did not play a kit for six months after OK Computer; then lessons with Bob Armstrong 'to work on technique and get a better grasp of a lot of different styles'. 'I'm not a session musician-type player, [but] I have done is develop quite a distinctive style.' The National Anthem's rhythm track came from a jam with Yorke, looped in sections of about 16 bars. No 'real' drums on Idioteque on record; he plays it live. Premier drums since the band's gear was stolen in the mid-1990s; a Premier Signia set in the rehearsal room. 'The sound of the drums has to be right for each song.' The magazine on Paranoid Android: 'Phil's restrained cross-sticking for much of the first three minutes, after which a brisk run around the toms ... until the choir comes in and the cross-sticking returns'; on Airbag: 'cut-up DJ Shadow-esque loops'; on Creep: 'disciplined simplicity'.

title: This Music Made Me: Philip Selway (musicOMH, 2015)
notes: His records: Lou Reed's Transformer and The Velvet Underground & Nico on one cassette; The Beat's I Just Can't Stop It (2 Tone 'a very formative scene'); Nick Drake's Bryter Layter; Juana Molina's Son; Mark Hollis; Joy Division's Unknown Pleasures: 'it was influential for me, as I think I have borrowed quite a bit from Stephen Morris's drumming over the years'; Bowie's Low; Bob Marley and the Wailers' Burnin' ('the best groove ever').

title: Pablo Honey - Wikipedia
notes: Released 22 February 1993 (Parlophone); recorded 1992 at Chipping Norton and Courtyard Studios, Oxfordshire; produced by Sean Slade, Paul Q. Kolderie and Chris Hufford. Philip Selway drums.

title: The Bends (album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 13 March 1995; recorded February-November 1994 at RAK, The Manor and Abbey Road, produced by John Leckie (Nigel Godrich engineering). Selway: recorded in about four months. Planet Telex began with a drum loop taken from the B-side Killer Cars. Just a single from 21 August 1995, number 19.

title: OK Computer - Wikipedia
notes: Released 21 May 1997; recorded July 1996 - March 1997 at Canned Applause, St Catherine's Court (Bath) and The Church; produced by Nigel Godrich and Radiohead. Airbag's beat is 'built from a seconds-long recording of Selway's drumming', influenced by DJ Shadow. Selway: 'We give each other an awful lot of space to develop our parts, but at the same time we are all very critical about what the other person is doing.'

title: Hail to the Thief - Wikipedia
notes: Released 9 June 2003; recorded September 2002 - early 2003 at Ocean Way, Hollywood, and the band's Oxfordshire studio, produced by Godrich. 'Prominent use of live drums' after Kid A and Amnesiac, which Selway called 'manufacturing music in the studio'; 2 + 2 = 5 opens on a sequenced drum pattern in 7/8. Selway: rock and electronic music 'the two hemispheres of the Radiohead brain'.

title: In Rainbows - Wikipedia
notes: Released 10 October 2007 (self-released, pay what you want); recorded February 2005 - June 2007 at Halswell House, Tottenham House and elsewhere, produced by Godrich. Videotape's live arrangement built on Selway's drums; on the album a TR-909. Selway and O'Brien later named it their favourite Radiohead album: 'everything that we'd been learning over two decades'.

title: Creep (Radiohead song) - Wikipedia
notes: Recorded as a warm-up the band did not know was being taped; Selway: 'The reason it sounds so powerful is because it's completely unselfconscious.' Philip Selway drums.

title: Paranoid Android - Wikipedia
notes: Four sections in 4/4, 'several three-bar segments in the second section ... in 7/8'; the opening at 82 BPM; the third section, written by Jonny Greenwood, at 62 BPM.

title: Karma Police - Wikipedia
notes: From the intro into a mid-tempo section alternating verse and chorus; Yorke and Godrich reconstructed the ending with loops and samples.

title: 15 Step - Wikipedia
notes: Developed in 2005; Yorke arranged it on his laptop, inspired by the 'clapping groove' of Peaches's Fuck the Pain Away. In 5/4, 'with a stuttering pattern played on a drum machine', and a 40-second 'mulched-up' drum introduction; handclaps by children of the Matrix Music School.
